subject: Hosted API pricing & volume qualification — post-call recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API pricing & volume qualification — post-call recap

Alex — thanks for taking the call earlier. Per our conversation, I wanted to summarize the key items we discussed and confirm a few numbers so we can put together a tailored hosted-API pricing proposal and next-steps.

Recap (from our discovery):
- Expected monthly token volume (in scope): ~120M–200M tokens, with a most-likely volume around 150M tokens/month.
- Peak concurrency / TPS: you mentioned traffic spikes roughly in the 20–35 TPS range, with steady-state closer to ~8–12 TPS.
- Primary workload: real-time chat and short-form generation (responses ~150–300 tokens on average).
- Key priorities: predictable unit economics, consistent 99th percentile latency under 500ms, and flexibility to burst for marketing spikes.

Pricing/PU target we discussed: you indicated a target of roughly $1,000–$1,500 per 1M tokens as a budgetary range for the hosted API — please confirm if that still holds.

Attachments: I’m attaching a preliminary pricing slide (redwood-hosted-api-pricing-v1.pdf) and the token forecast template (acme-token-forecast.xlsx) so you can drop in any revised numbers.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm: expected monthly tokens (best estimate), expected peak TPS for a sustained 5–10 minute window, and any hard budget targets ($/1M tokens)?
2) If numbers align, we’ll draft a 6-month proof-of-value proposal with committed monthly tokens and burst allowances.
3) Proposed follow-up: 30-min call next week to review the draft (I’m available Tue/Wed afternoon PST).

Thanks — I’ll wait for your updated forecast and budget confirmation and will loop in Rishi for pricing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0124

Attachment: redwood-hosted-api-pricing-v1.pdf
Attachment: acme-token-forecast.xlsx

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-ai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme-ai.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing & volume qualification — post-call recap

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary. A few confirmations from our side: 

- Monthly volume: our conservative estimate is 120M tokens/month, upside to 200M if adoption picks up — planning number to use: 150M tokens/month.
- Peak TPS: during promotional campaigns we see short spikes up to ~30–35 TPS for ~5–10 minutes. Normal peak is ~20–25 TPS.
- Average response size: ~200 tokens.
- Budget target: we’re aiming for roughly $1,000–$1,500 per 1M tokens for hosted API at scale. If you can get us into the low end of that range with a committed discount, that would be ideal.

We can share the product traffic spreadsheet if you want more granular hourly breakdowns — I’ve attached our internal forecast as discussed.

Next: let’s plan the follow-up review after you put together the proposal. Maria (cc) is our finance lead — she’ll want the committed vs burst pricing and a total monthly cost projection.

Appreciate it,
Alex Turner
Head of Product
Acme AI
alex.turner@acme-ai.com

Attachment: acme-token-forecast-filled.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme-ai.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing & volume qualification — post-call recap

Alex — great, thanks for confirming. I’ve reviewed the attached forecast and it’s helpful to have the hourly shape (that drives the batching/cache economics on our side). A few quick clarifying Qs before we build the proposal: 

- For the 150M/mo case, is that net tokens (input+output) or output-only? Please confirm so we size costs correctly.
- For peak TPS, can you confirm whether the 30–35 TPS is sustained for multiple consecutive minutes (e.g., 5–10) or is it typically single-minute bursts? This will affect concurrency sizing.
- Any compliance/regulatory constraints (EU data residency, SOC 2 evidence) that we should include in the proposal?

Draft proposal plan: I’ll put together a 6-month committed offering with a tiered unit price (committed vs burst) plus a modeled monthly cost table at three volume points (120M / 150M / 200M). I’ll share the draft pricing PDF ahead of our call.

Proposed times for a 30-min review: Wed 18 Feb 11:00–12:30 PST or Thu 19 Feb 14:00–16:00 PST. Which works best for you?

Thanks — looping Rishi for pricing calibration and to include engineering if we need to confirm latency SLOs.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-hosted-api-pricing-v1.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: ACME pricing guidance (do not share comps)

Internal note — pricing guidance based on the 150M/mo estimate and peak ~30 TPS: 

- Recommend a committed 6-month tier: $1,100 per 1M tokens for committed volume (min 100M/mo commit).
- Burst/overage rate: $1,600 per 1M tokens for tokens above committed baseline (short-term bursts allowed up to 2x baseline for up to 30 minutes without additional infra charge).
- Engineering: We can hit 99th pct latency <500ms at this concurrency on hosted API with our burst autoscaling configuration; call out that very sustained >40 TPS will require Dedicated or capacity reservation.
- Include a one-time POC credit (50% off first-month committed delta) and 30-day SLA trial for first 3 months as a close incentive.

I’ve attached a redlined pricing PDF for the proposal draft. Please incorporate these numbers and the modeled cost table; Marissa — confirm the final proposed times and I’ll join the review.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-hosted-api-pricing-v1.pdf
